stateEmploymentOverview.note: Rural columns come from the agricultural land-use ledger (staple crop labor plus hunting, fishing, viticulture, and husbandry). Independent growth spends leftover adults on extra fields after reserving this year's child→adult outflow. Megacity keeps ~32% of rural adults as an urban-bound pool while the rest develop as much hinterland as they can tend, so a cell can ship both people and grain. Harvest peaks draw household helpers and neighbour mutual aid. Urban columns exclude household care. Surplus is unassigned adults — outflow / the megacity migrant pool, not idle harvest hands.
stateEmploymentOverview.emptyState: No State has recorded rural or urban demographics yet.

about.costOfLivingIntro: This world uses one shared coinage: gold pieces 🟡, silver pieces ⚪, and copper pieces 🟤. Prices, treasury balances, and personal wealth are stored as silver-piece values and displayed as coinage. Grain trades at roughly one silver piece per wain at market (farmgate prices run about 20% lower), anchoring the currency's baseline value. The figures below are storytelling guidelines, not exact simulated totals; actual prices vary with local market conditions.
about.costOfLivingPeasant: One peasant (rural resident), bare subsistence for a year: roughly 4–5 copper pieces at the default exchange rates — just enough grain to survive, based on the world's per-capita food need.
about.costOfLivingUrban: One town or city resident, for a year: roughly 5–10 copper pieces at the default exchange rates — the same baseline food need, plus higher retail prices and incidental goods city life requires.
about.costOfLivingFamily: One family of four or five, for a year: roughly 2–4 silver pieces — the sum of each member's living cost.
about.costOfLivingHouse: A modest house or homestead: roughly 10–30 silver pieces — several years of a laborer's savings. Buying property isn't a simulated transaction yet, so treat this as a storytelling rule of thumb rather than an in-game price.

generation.headingTip: Map generation settings. Generate a new map to apply the settings
generation.canvasSizeTip: Set original map size on generation. It cannot be changed later. Always keep canvas size equal to your screen size or less.
generation.mapSeedTip: Map seed number. Press 'Enter' or click the play button to generate a new map with this seed
generation.showSeedHistory: Show seed history to apply a previous seed
generation.generateWithSeed: Generate a new map with this seed
generation.copySeed: Copy map seed as URL. It will produce the same map only if options are default or the same
generation.pointsNumberTip: Set number of points to be used for graph generation. Highly affects performance. 10K is the only recommended value
generation.heightmapTip: Select heightmap template to be used for map generation
generation.randomHeightmapPoolTip: When Heightmap is unlocked, limit random selection to templates with the selected average land or ocean coverage
generation.economyStartTip: Starting capital and ordinary upkeep for Economy. Balanced is the default pre-gunpowder setting: cities begin able to function, while routine administration and market maintenance absorb most ordinary revenue. Generate a new map to apply.
generation.biomeRegionTip: Regional climate-vegetation profile: adjusts continuous great forests, heath mosaics, mediterranean scrub, mangroves, and mountain biomes without replacing the base terrain generator. Applies immediately, no regenerate needed.
generation.volcanismChanceTip: Chance that a single, dominant mountain peak becomes a tagged volcano (distinct barren/lava biome, auto-selected volcano icon) instead of an ordinary summit, decided while the heightmap itself is built. Checked once per qualifying peak, so even 100% rarely produces more than a handful of volcanoes on one map. 0 disables volcano tagging entirely. Unlike Biome region/Volcanic soil strength below, this decides where volcanoes sit on the terrain, so it needs the heightmap re-rolled to apply: press Regenerate climate and waterways during stage review (it re-runs Landscape first, same seed), Generate another landscape, or generate a new map. The rest of the terrain stays exactly as it was — only volcano tagging changes.
generation.activeVolcanoChanceTip: Of the volcanoes actually generated, the share that are active — a molten crater (Lava field biome) — rather than dormant, whose summit is instead carved into a crater lake (Volcanic barrens biome around it). Decided alongside heightmap generation, same as Volcanism chance — press Regenerate climate and waterways during stage review, Generate another landscape, or generate a new map to apply.
generation.volcanicSoilStrengthTip: How far the fertile Volcanic soil biome ring extends down an already-tagged volcano's flanks before yielding to the ordinary climate biome. 0 keeps only the barren crater; 100 spreads rich farmland far down the slope. Only rescales an existing per-cell intensity value, so — unlike the two options above — this applies immediately, no regenerate needed.
generation.enclosureCalculationTip: How harbor/mooring calmness (pack.cells.enclosure) is scored for ocean-connected water. Ocean Currents reads the resolved current speed at the shoreline itself — bends around headlands and funnels out of bays/straits, but almost every shore cell reads near-zero regardless of real shelter, so it saturates toward 100 close to the coast. Ocean Currents (Ambient) instead reads the current speed a short distance offshore, distinguishing a genuinely sheltered bay from an exposed open coastline — better for siting decisions like harbor placement. Both score every lake cell fully enclosed. Radius is the legacy fixed 6-hop land-blocked-ratio heuristic for all. Applies immediately, no regenerate needed.
generation.oceanCurrentRenderingTip: How the Ocean Currents WebGL layer draws grid.cells.currentAngle/currentSpeed. Direction Lines draws a short arrow per cell, colored by water temperature — cells reading exactly 0 speed are skipped, so a calm patch looks like a gap. Intensity Shading instead fills every ocean cell by current speed alone (pale = calm, dark = strong), with full gapless coverage. Applies immediately, no regenerate needed.
generation.culturesNumberTip: Define how many Cultures should be generated
generation.culturesSetTip: Select a set of cultures to be used for names and cultures generation
generation.raceSettingsTip: Configure race name spheres, the character ability system, and races available to new characters. Opens a dialog so Generation stays short.
generation.initialPopulationTip: Determines how full the world is relative to its carrying capacity at the start. 100% means fully saturated, lower values allow for future demographic growth.
generation.settlementPatternTip: Choose whether initial people are spread across suitable land or concentrated around favorable settlement hubs. Selecting a preset also applies its recommended initial population percentage. Marches sits between Frontier and Scattered: several polity islands with wilderness/danger between them.
generation.oikoumeneLandShareTip: Target share of suitable land capacity that becomes the oikoumene (settled / state-claimable core). Lower = more wilderness and shorter interstate borders; higher = larger realms. Ignored for Standard (full habitable fill). Fantasy defaults ~45%.
generation.burgsNumberTip: Define a number of non-capital settlements to be placed (if enough suitable land exists)
generation.statesNumberTip: Define the number of states for standard maps
generation.polityDensityTip: Define polity density for settlement-network maps
generation.frontierStartModeTip: How frontier states begin. Land origin is humanity arising here: capitals sit on large landmasses, nobody has ships yet, and no sea lanes are charted. Seaborne landing beaches each state on a large coast with ships and sea lanes between those ports. One-cell isles are never starting homelands; islands remain valid later as colonies.
generation.frontierPolitySpacingTip: How far apart Frontier capitals start. Spread apart (default) gives each state its own distant homeland so they do not open next to each other. Clustered keeps the earlier close start, with several states sharing one settlement cluster.
generation.initialPolityRealmSizeTip: How many land cells each state owns at generation. 1 is the capital only (one city). Higher values grow a compact core around the capital, up to 30 cells, and stay inside the oikoumene. Oikoumene land share still decides how much countryside is populated; this slider only decides how much of it starts as state land.
generation.sizeVarietyTip: Define how much states and cultures can vary in size. Defines expansionism value
generation.growthRateTip: Set state and cultures growth rate. Defines how many lands will stay neutral
generation.provincesRatioTip: Set what share of eligible burgs in each state will become province centers. Higher values create more provinces
generation.historyAttemptsTip: Define how many times wars are generated to build relations history.
generation.religionsNumberTip: Define how many organized religions and cults should be generated. Cultures will have their own folk religions in any case
generation.mapNameTip: Define map name (will be used to name downloaded files)
generation.yearAndEraTip: Define current year and era name
generation.historicalPeriodTip: Select the historical-technology backdrop. Drives water/sanitation tech ceilings and other period-flavored generation choices; gunpowder-era Goods/military units are controlled separately in Military Options.
generation.startFirearmsUnstockedTip: New maps normally treat existing musketeer and artillery units as already equipped. Enable this to start their firearm equipment at zero and require state procurement through the economy.
generation.stateLabelsTip: Select state labels mode: display short or full names
generation.ironDepositsPerStateTip: Minimum number of iron-bearing deposits generated per active state. The normal geological distribution remains unchanged; compatible iron deposits are added only if it would otherwise fall below this target. 0.40 is the balanced default, leaving iron as a tradable strategic resource. Generate a new map to apply.
generation.faunaPopulationModelTip: Detail level of the fauna population model backing Game and livestock production. Detailed runs an annual per-cell wildlife/livestock cohort model (breeding, aging, age-selective culling, carrying capacity) that caps output by an actual headcount instead of an unlimited rate. Simplified skips that model and keeps the cheaper labour/rate-gated formula with no population ceiling — a performance option for large maps. Apply on next map generation.

simulation.heading: Simulation Settings:
simulation.headingTip: Settings related to time advancement and demographics simulation
simulation.baseBirthRateTip: Base birth rate per female adult per year at zero population density. Higher values mean faster demographic recovery and higher equilibrium limits.
simulation.childMortalityTip: Child mortality rate. The percentage of children who die before reaching adulthood. A historically realistic rate is 20-40%. 0% causes rapid population spikes.
simulation.conflictAutonomyTip: Autonomous lets rulers begin wars as time advances. Player-directed prevents automatic declarations, battles, and occupations while economic and demographic simulation continues.
simulation.warFrequencyTip: Multiplier for how quickly autonomous wars mature. 1.0 is default (wars take roughly a generation to brew). 0.0 prevents autonomous escalation. 2.0 means frequent wars.
simulation.currencyHeadingTip: Display-only coin denominations. Internal prices, treasuries, and personal wealth remain stored as silver-piece values.
simulation.goldToSilverTip: How many silver pieces equal one gold piece. This changes display only.
simulation.silverToCopperTip: How many copper pieces equal one silver piece. This changes display only.
simulation.systemsHeadingTip: Toggle advance-time subsystems. Day is the base unit (Month ≈ 30.5 days, Year ≈ 365). Turn off unused systems to speed up long runs.
simulation.demographicsTip: Aging, births, migration, and overpopulation losses each advance tick
simulation.manpowerLedgerTip: Civilian adult males ↔ troops under arms: draft, refill, demobilize, and non-double-counted battle deaths
simulation.settlementGrowthTip: Independent: each settlement grows toward its own capacity via births only, no deliberate labor movement. Megacity: rural cells also release labor-safety-margined surplus adults once a year toward nearby cities (requires Economy enabled).
simulation.militaryRecoveryTip: Regiment reinforcement and cleanup of destroyed units (uses manpower pool when Manpower ledger is on)
simulation.recruitQualityTip: New recruits dilute regiment quality; combat power scales with quality (green troops fight poorly)
simulation.femaleLevyTip: When male adults are scarce, draft a limited share of adult females into under-arms (experimental)

extensionsTab.skipTradeTip: Defers global trade-route matching and caravan spawning (the Trade layer/animation's data) when preparing a freshly generated map's economy, so the map stays interactive sooner. Re-run it later from Tools > Economy > Regenerate > Production. This is a standing preference, not locked per generation.
extensionsTab.characterBiasTip: Skews every character Nobility creates or replaces (rulers, central officers, field/fleet officers, province lords, and successions): young age, a high Appearance score, and a lopsided gender ratio favoring the chosen gender. A race with a hard gender lock (e.g. Amazones) is unaffected. This is a standing preference, applied to every future generation and succession — not a one-time reroll of the current roster.

regenerate.title: Regenerate {{feature}}
regenerate.body: Regenerate will remove all the custom changes for the {{feature}}.
regenerate.confirm: Are you sure you want to proceed?
regenerate.seaNote: The improved mode restores nearby Delaunay connections and keeps a separate coastal port backbone.
regenerate.landNote: Elevation-aware mode prefers gentler climbs; mountain passes still connect when no lowland corridor exists. Tune the aversion slider below.
regenerate.elevationAversionNote: 0 allows short ridge shortcuts (e.g. ~500 m climbs between nearby burgs). 1 is the default. Higher values force longer valley detours. Sole passes still connect when no alternative exists.
regenerate.internationalDefaultNote: Preserves the settlement pattern's historic cross-border route behavior.
regenerate.internationalPeacefulNote: Adds one land trail and one sea lane per shared feature for neighboring states that are allied, friendly, neutral, or in a vassal relationship.
regenerate.internationalAllAdjacentNote: Adds low-grade trails and sea lanes for every neighboring state pair, including enemies. It never creates cross-border roads.
regenerate.internationalNoneNote: Does not add automatic cross-border trails or sea lanes.
regenerate.seedMix: Mix map seed with current time
regenerate.seedNote: Map seed always rebuilds the same rulers and officers. Mix with time or use a fresh seed when you want a different roster without regenerating the whole map.
